items.title: A tuple becomes a direct summand inclusion after inverting some element of the complement of a point exactly when its image generates an independent family of the fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement compares two conditions for a tuple s_1, ..., s_r of elements of a module M in a fixed situation over a scheme: that the tuple becomes the inclusion of a direct summand after inverting some element f outside a point x, and that the images of the tuple in the fibre V(x) are linearly independent (statement lines 38730-38746). The proof introduces a perpendicular B(x) inside the fibre M(x) together with its quotient V(x), shows that the evaluation maps realise all linear forms on V(x), and then runs the two directions: independence in V(x) produces a dual family whose composite with the tuple has a determinant outside x, while a splitting after inverting f is turned into dual maps over R by clearing denominators through the localization behaviour of Hom from a finitely presented module (proof lines 38749-38785). The subtle point is the passage from maps over the localization back to maps over R, which is what makes the equivalence canonical. The counted span refers to the situation of the section and to one lemma of another chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
